reason: The vacuity claim is true and I reproduced every number in it; the proposed fix is wrong against the real source, and by the brief's own rule that is a refutation. VERIFIED: open() (interaction-check.mjs:76-79) waits 1800ms; .bar animates grow 0.5s on a delay of i*40ms+340ms (lately.html:255-256), so the twelfth column is done at 1280ms. Driven at 1440x960 in chromium, the first .bar measures 70.55px at 1800ms on ?state=full&v=light (data-motion='settled') and 70.55px at 1800ms on ?state=full&v=light&motion=play, so ok(...still.h > 8) at line 513 returns the same true with the override honoured and with it switched off. I also checked the other five open() calls that omit reducedMotion (446, 463, 554, 1199, 1357): all sample at >=1800ms, and every one of the other 56 passes reducedMotion:true, which forces 1ms/0ms through the prefers-reduced-motion block at lately.html:536 — a different mechanism from the settled block at 542. So the seat is right that line 507's attribute check is the only witness the override has and nothing measures its effect. THE FIX IS WHERE IT FAILS. It says to sample 'inside the first animation frame after load' and assert the settled bar is '>= 60px at 1440x960'. Driven three times, the settled page at the FIRST rAF after load reports the .bar animation at currentTime 0 with playState 'running' and a measured height of 0.00px in two runs of three (70.55px in the third); the backwards half of the `both` fill is still in force on that frame, and the height only resolves to 70.55px on the second rAF. The assertion as specified therefore fails against the correct, currently-shipping implementation about two times in three: it would replace an assertion that cannot fail with one that fails at random on green code, which is a worse outcome than the one it fixes and would have to be reverted. The play half (<= 1px at the same instant) is sound — play holds 0.00px for the full 340ms delay, ~20 frames. The severity class is right for the underlying problem: the surface is not wrong, the evidence for it is, so defect, not misleading.
sharpenedFix: Same shape, corrected instant and a loud guard instead of a race. Keep line 507. Replace line 509-513 with a paired sample taken at a fixed 150ms after load on two pages — not at the first animation frame, which lands before the settled animation has advanced past currentTime 0 and reads 0.00px. (a) goto ?state=full&v=light, await page.waitForTimeout(150), read h = document.querySelector('.bar').getBoundingClientRect().height and assert h >= 60 (measured 70.55px; the fixture would have to change for this to move). (b) goto ?state=full&v=light&motion=play, await the same 150ms, assert the same bar measures <= 1px (measured 0.00px, and the delay does not expire until 340ms, so the margin is ~190ms). (c) Guard the sample so a slow machine fails visibly rather than silently: on the play page read a = bar.getAnimations()[0] at the same instant and ok('the play sample lands inside the entrance', a.currentTime < 300, `${a.currentTime}ms`) — if that fails, (b) is not evidence of anything and the gate says so. Optionally add the direct CSSOM witness alongside it, which cannot race at all: on the settled page assert bar.getAnimations()[0].effect.getTiming() reports duration 1 and delay 0, and on the play page 500 and 340 (both confirmed by measurement). Rename line 513 to what it now proves, e.g. 'settled has the columns up before the entrance could have run, and play does not'.
breaks: The corrected check adds two page loads plus 300ms to the gate — trivial against 461 assertions. What it couples to: the 60px floor is fixture-derived (first week of state=full at 1440x960 = 70.55px), so derive-fixture.mjs changing week 1's value moves it — floor it well under the real number, as 60 does, or read the expected height from window.LATELY_FIXTURE rather than hard-coding. The 150ms sample and the 300ms guard are tied to the 340ms delay at lately.html:256; if that delay is ever shortened below ~250ms both halves must be re-measured. Re-measure after it lands: run interaction-check.mjs five times to confirm the play-side guard never trips on this machine, and confirm the settled half still reads 70.55px under reducedMotion:'reduce' as well as without it, since the media-query block at lately.html:536 and the settled block at 542 both apply on a machine set to reduce and the check must not quietly start proving the media query instead of the override.
